01/11/2026 DRAFT
Title: Non-governmental organisation regulation in Niger and Mali
Subtitle: Global Humanitarian Overview (GHO) 2027 context for the child protection cluster
Contribution: Context Analysis and Foresight Unit (CAFU) Strategic Analysis, evidence cut-off 31/10/2026

BLUF
Permission to operate tightened in Niger and stalled in Mali during 2025. Niger suspended non-compliant non-governmental organisation (NGO) activities on 15/11/2025 and later reported dissolutions and a review of over 3,000 structures. Mali stopped 17 projects awaiting No Objection Notices in 2025, with no new NGO law found in the gazettes read. We judge child protection delivery will shrink where authorisations lapse. Teams should track authorisation lists and notice lead times.

Core text (150 words)
In Niger the Interior Ministry ordered on 15/11/2025 the suspension of NGOs and associations that had not published their 2024 financial statements in the Official Gazette. About 140 organisations were listed as authorised to continue. The order followed a forum on NGO operations held on 29/10/2025–31/10/2025 in Tillabéri. Later posts reported dissolutions on 07/01/2026 and a compliance review covering over 3,000 structures, with 1,684 national and 125 international NGOs authorised. In Mali no new NGO law was found in the Official Gazettes read for 31/12/2025 and 21/08/2026. Bureaucratic blocks stopped work: 17 projects awaiting No Objection Notices, including 12 humanitarian projects, were not implemented in 2025. Children face effects. In Niger 1,500,000 children required urgent assistance in 2025, including 304,463 children displaced by conflict. Nearly 779 schools stayed closed for insecurity, affecting more than 66,000 children. Mali recorded 814 access incidents in 2025, up 41% from 574 in 2024.

Evidence and confidence
Tags: SOLID needs primary text read plus one independent report. REPORTED means press only or single source. JUDGEMENT marks our assessment with we judge. TO CHECK means searched and not found.

- REPORTED: National forum on association operations 29/10/2025 to 31/10/2025 in Tillabéri stressed financial transparency and regular accountability. Interior Ministry note to regional governors, announced 15/11/2025 via national radio, suspended activities of non-governmental organisations and associations that had not published 2024 financial statements in the Official Gazette. About 140 organisations listed as authorised to continue. Stated aim: regulate associative interventions. Actor named: Minister of State, Minister of Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration Mohamed Toumba. Primary note not read. Reporting source: British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) News Afrique dispatch 23/11/2025, page text only (https://www.bbc.com/afrique/articles/cy5qxpq5357o). Supporting social excerpt notes suspension of hundreds of organisations (https://www.facebook.[masqué]%C3%A8re-de-lint%C3%A9rieur-nig%C3%A9rien-a-ordonn%C3%A9-la-suspension-des-/[masqué]). Gazette reference not found.
- REPORTED: Dissolution decisions announced 07/01/2026 against several non-compliant organisations. Separate compliance review claims over 3,000 structures counted, with 1,684 national and 125 international non-governmental organisations recognised as compliant and authorised to continue. Full texts not read. Review date and coverage not stated. Figures conflict with 140 authorised on 15/11/2025. Gap unresolved. Single excerpt sources: dissolution post (https://www.facebook.[masqué]%C3%A9er-letat/[masqué]) and review post (https://www.facebook.com/maliactu/posts/niger-grand-m%C3%[masqué]).
- REPORTED: National masterclass on personal data protection held 22/07/2026 at Hotel Bravia in Niamey for non-governmental organisation delegates. Organiser: SOS Children's Villages in Niger. Attendance: over 45 representatives of national and international non-governmental organisations, data experts, cyber security specialists and national institutions. Speakers named: executive bureau vice-president Idriss Eko and project team leader Cheffou Maman Sani. Purpose: strengthen data governance, regulatory compliance and cyber security for sensitive child and family data. Source: Nigerien Press Agency report, full text read (https://anp.[masqué]). No second independent source in dossier.
- REPORTED: Official Gazettes read show no non-governmental organisation regulation text in retrieved extracts. Gazette Number 35 dated 31/12/2025, full text read, contains architect profession law, public establishment law, police and civil protection ordinances and mining and appointment decrees. Gazette Number 19 dated 21/08/2026, page text only, contains loan ordinances, school infrastructure, textile company, village statute and family code amendment. Full series sweep not completed. Primary sources: (https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2025/mali-jo-2025-35.pdf) and (https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2026/mali-jo-2026-19.pdf).
- REPORTED: Mali 2025 access blocks include administrative holds. A total of 17 projects awaiting No Objection Notices, including 12 humanitarian projects and 5 development projects, were not implemented. A total of 814 access incidents recorded in 2025, up 41% from 574 in 2024. Explosive devices: 355 cases, up 18% from 2024. Violence against personnel, property and infrastructure: at least 71 incidents, up 22% from 58 in 2024, in Gao, Bamako, Ségou and Mopti. Movement restrictions for personnel and goods: 28 cases, up 22% from 23 in 2024, mostly irregular checks in Mopti and Ségou. Humanitarian funding rate: 20% in 2025, down from 44% in 2024, with programme suspensions and staff reductions. Source: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) yearly dashboard published 05/02/2026, full text read (https://reliefweb.[masqué]). No independent second source in dossier.
- REPORTED: Monthly sequence shows volatility and southward spread. During 01/08/2025 to 31/08/2025, 58 access incidents, down 29% from 82 during 01/07/2025 to 31/07/2025, with 34 explosive device cases. Gossi restrictions eased from 26/08/2025. During 01/11/2025 to 30/11/2025, 37 incidents, down 27% from 51 during 01/10/2025 to 31/10/2025, with 12 interference and movement cases. Léré placed under restrictions again during 01/10/2025 to 31/10/2025, with 15 other localities hard to reach. National roads (RN) affected include RN33 between Ségou and Niono, RN6 between Sévaré and San, RN7, RN10 and RN20 between Ménaka and Ansongo. Coordinated attacks 25/04/2026 hit Bamako, the international airport, Kati, Sévaré, Gao and Kidal. Senou displaced persons site in Bamako destroyed and looted, including a Child-Friendly Space supported for 4 years. Movement limits around Bamako and isolation of Douentza and Bandiagara reported, with suspension of flights. Sources: OCHA August dashboard (https://reliefweb.[masqué]), OCHA November dashboard, full texts read (https://www.unocha.[masqué]), and flash update 30/04/2026 published 11/05/2026, page text only (https://reliefweb.[masqué]).
- REPORTED: Niger 2025 needs centre on children. A total of 2,600,000 people, including 1,500,000 children, require urgent assistance. Displaced people totalled 929,247 at 31/12/2024, mostly due to conflict. Conflict displacement totalled 507,438 people, including 304,463 children. Health coverage stands at 55.5%, leaving around 6,000,000 children without regular care, notably in Tillabéry, Diffa, Tahoua and Maradi. Wasting cases projected at 1,800,000 for 2025. Nearly 779 schools remain closed due to insecurity, affecting over 66,000 children and 1,700 teachers. Floods damaged 5,520 classrooms. Funding need totals US$101,700,000, with 81.2% for nutrition, education, health, child protection and water, sanitation and hygiene. Source: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) Humanitarian Action for Children 2025 Niger, published 08/12/2025, full text read (https://reliefweb.[masqué]). No independent second source in dossier.
- JUDGEMENT: We judge authorisation losses in Niger and notice holds in Mali will cut child protection presence first where needs already peak. Basis: 304,463 displaced children, 779 closed schools and 55.5% health coverage in Niger, plus 17 stalled projects and 814 incidents in Mali during 2025. Data gap: number of child protection projects among suspended and stalled caseloads not found.

How access narrows
Niger publication filter. Organisations absent from the authorised list must stop activities. Referral, case management and family support capacity drops by administrative decision.
Mali notice filter. Projects without a No Objection Notice do not start. Protection and education inputs stall even where roads allow passage.
Children protection gap. Loss of authorised partners and safe spaces reduces reporting, psychosocial support and school linkage. Displaced children and pupils from closed schools face longer service gaps.

Conditional scenarios
Scenario 1 Extended enforcement in Niger. Trigger: Interior Ministry releases an updated authorised list after the 07/01/2026 dissolutions. Indicator: share of tracked child protection partners on the authorised list falls by 10% or more within 60 days of release.
Scenario 2 Notice backlog persists in Mali. Trigger: 2025 pending notices remain uncleared during 01/01/2026 to 31/03/2026. Indicator: fewer than 50% of tracked No Objection Notice requests clear within 60 days of submission.

Critical unknowns
- TO CHECK: Legal instrument number, signature date, Official Gazette reference, exact deadline for 2024 statements, scope and exemptions for the 15/11/2025 suspension. Searched by Nova on 01/11/2026, not found in dossier.
- TO CHECK: Date, coverage and full authorised lists reconciling 140 organisations on 15/11/2025 with 1,684 national and 125 international organisations in later review. Searched by Nova on 01/11/2026, not found in dossier.
- TO CHECK: Full text of 07/01/2026 dissolution decisions, names of organisations, appeal process and duration. Searched by Nova on 01/11/2026, not found in dossier.
- TO CHECK: Mali No Objection Notice issuing authority, statutory lead time, 2026 backlog total and clearance rate. Searched by Nova on 01/11/2026, not found in dossier.
- TO CHECK: Number of child protection projects and children directly losing services due to suspensions and notice holds in Niger and Mali. Searched by Nova on 01/11/2026, not found in dossier.

Recommendations
1. Maintain a dated matrix of Niger partner authorisation status against each official list release, with service coverage noted per site.
2. Log each Mali No Objection Notice request with submission date, authority, follow-up dates and outcome, and escalate files pending over 30 days.
3. Duplicate anonymised child protection case summaries and referral maps across 2 locations and pre-agree 2 alternative referral paths per site.

Limitations
Evidence cut-off 31/10/2026. Primary texts read in full: OCHA Mali yearly dashboard published 05/02/2026, OCHA dashboards covering 01/08/2025 to 31/08/2025 and 01/11/2025 to 30/11/2025, UNICEF Niger appeal published 08/12/2025, Nigerien Press Agency report dated 22/07/2026, Mali Official Gazette Number 35 dated 31/12/2025. Page text only: Mali Official Gazette Number 19 dated 21/08/2026, BBC dispatch 23/11/2025, Mali flash update 30/04/2026. Excerpts only: 3 social posts on suspensions, dissolutions and review. Not read: Interior Ministry note to governors, dissolution decisions, full gazette series. No specialist regulatory analysis for Niger or Mali in dossier. Mali children in need total not found. Authorised counts from 15/11/2025 and later review not reconciled.

Overall 7.0/10. Mean 3.5 times 2. No dimension below 3/5.

Spark Open QA review (open-weight Meta model on Baseten, after drafting by Spark 1.3)
1) Facts:
- 814 is 41.8% above 574, not 41% — rounding understates the increase by about 5 incidents.
- BLUF states "no new NGO law found in the gazettes read" as a general finding, while Evidence/Limitations qualify that only two extracts were read (Number 35 full text, Number 19 page text only) and "full series sweep not completed" — scope overstated in summary versus evidence.
- 17 projects are described as "stopped" in BLUF/Core text but as "were not implemented" while awaiting No Objection Notices in Evidence — started-then-halted versus never-started.

2) Tags:
- None found — all REPORTED bullets explicitly note single-source/press-only status or absence of a second independent report, consistent with the stated tag definitions and QA log downgrade; JUDGEMENT and TO CHECK bullets match their descriptions.

3) Score:
- Score: 6.5/10 — figures are traceable and dates are separated, but the unresolved 140 versus 1,809 authorised conflict, limited gazette sweep, and heavy reliance on single-source OCHA/UNICEF dashboards plus social excerpts weaken factual and sourcing strength. Disagree — the note's 7.0/10 is slightly generous.
